text:
jordan: Quick question — for streaming requests the gateway currently treats a connection-level retry window of 30s for aborted streams. Is the plan to preserve idempotency tokens across reconnects for resumable streams? I worry about double-execution on backend side. @samir @priya :thinking:
priya: We discussed 30s in the RFC but didn't finalize token scope. My vote: token tied to request-id + model-version + tenant; if session reconnects with same request-id within the window -> resume, otherwise it's a new request.
samir: +1 for tying to request-id. Also need to decide if KV cache is considered part of the resume semantics. If we resume, we must avoid reapplying side-effects (logs, billing). Suggest a gateway-level dedupe that drops duplicated finalization events.
kit: infra note — sticky session affinity makes resume easier but hurts failover. If we keep token state at edge, we need distributed cache with TTL (Redis/consul-style). Ops-bot will create a ticket for infra sizing.
ops-bot: Created ticket INF-7286: 'stream-resume-token-store' assigned to @kit, priority P2
priya: How do we signal to clients whether a stream was resumed vs replayed vs new? Header? trailer? I think trailers are cleaner for streaming so we don't inject messages mid-stream.
jordan: Agreed — use a trailer so the stream body is unchanged. Suggested trailer: X-Resume-Status: resumed|replayed|new and X-Resume-Reason: resumed_timeout|routed|conflict
samir: Implementation sketch:
```
// initial request headers
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
Resume-Token: <opaque>

// on reconnect
Resume-Token: <opaque>
```
Gateway checks token store, if token mapped to active session return 409 conflict OR we can wait for graceful closure. If token maps to stale session and KV-state exists -> perform resume. Return trailer with resume status.
kit: Concern: returning 409 on flaky mobile networks creates awful UX. Maybe return 200 and include Resume-Status: conflict plus hint to retry to a different node. But that hides the problem from clients.
priya: Alternate: always accept reconnect but mark resumed outputs as 'duplicate' and expose a replay flag in the API. That pushes complexity to backend services and product teams.
jordan: TL;DR proposal: 1) token scope = request-id + model + tenant; 2) default resume window = 60s (configurable per route); 3) token store = distributed cache with short TTL + leader-annotated session owner; 4) gateway emits trailer X-Resume-Status on stream close.
samir: Also: make retry policy orthogonal — retries that restart the request must provide a new idempotency key; only reconnects presenting the same resume-token are eligible to resume KV-state and avoid re-execution.
priya: I'll draft a follow-up RFC with sequence diagrams, state machine for token lifecycle, and sample headers/trailers. Will include migration notes for legacy clients. Assigning eng-runtime and eng-infra for micro-design. :thumbsup:
jordan: Thanks — can we slot a 20m sync in tomorrow's arch office hours for quick alignment?
priya: I'm in. samir?
samir: Yep
kit: I'll bring infra cost estimates.
jordan: Great, done.
